name: Bandhan: Targeting the Hardcore Poor (Founders Pledge, 2018)
summary: A graduation program in West Bengal, India: the poorest women get a productive asset (usually livestock), a small stipend, training and a year and a half of coaching. A re-implementation of Founders Pledge's 2018 cost-effectiveness analysis, based on the randomised trial's ten-year follow-up.

Cost to double consumption for one person for one year (USD)
rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's bottom line: $62 to double one person's consumption for a year ($41–134 across its conservative and optimistic cases). Doubling consumption is a rise of ln(2) in ln(consumption), so this is the cost per ln unit times ln(2).

rows.label: Doubled-income years per dollar
rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's cost to double one person's consumption for a year, turned around. One doubled-income year is one unit of value, the site's common unit, so nothing else converts.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: The midpoint of our defaults for programs that hand out goods (15%) and those where staff deliver the help (50%), rounded: a large part of the cost of a graduation or business-grant program is the asset or cash grant itself, the rest mostly staff time for training and mentoring. Our judgment; we haven't seen this program's breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Field staff and mentors at nonprofits often earn somewhat less than in comparable jobs. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Doubled-income years per donor dollar
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest).
